name: Rome
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Rome: procurement and concession diligence, Tribunale delle imprese support and Italian ownership research.
hero_lede: Rome is Italy's seat of government, national regulators, state-controlled groups and UN food agencies. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the capital, working from public records and coordinating licensed Italian investigators and the client's counsel where local work is required.
intro: Rome is Italy's capital and largest municipality, with about 2.7 million residents in the comune and more in the wider Metropolitan City of Rome Capital. Its economy is dominated by services: central government and public administration, national regulators and agencies, the headquarters of several large state-controlled and formerly state-owned groups in energy, infrastructure, defence and telecommunications, banking and insurance, construction, real estate, film and media, and tourism. Rome also hosts the United Nations food and agriculture agencies and many embassies, including those accredited to the Holy See. Fiumicino airport is the country's main international gateway, while Italy's stock exchange is in Milan rather than Rome.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Rome because public money and regulatory decisions are concentrated there. Companies bidding for national contracts, concessions or infrastructure work need to assess consortium partners, subcontractors and intermediaries for corruption, conflict-of-interest and organised crime infiltration risk. Investors in Roman real estate, hospitality and media need to understand layered ownership through fiduciary companies and holding structures. Disputes with Italian state-linked counterparties, administrative challenges and corporate litigation before the Rome business court frequently require evidence about people, companies and assets in the city. Rome's role as a centre of diplomacy and international organisations adds further cross-border dimensions.

matters.title: Procurement and concession partner diligence
matters.text: National contracts and concessions are awarded largely by ministries and agencies in Rome. We examine consortium partners, subcontractors and advisers for ownership, related parties, criminal or anti-mafia measures reported publicly, administrative litigation and press coverage before bids, teaming agreements or acquisitions.

matters.title: State-linked counterparty research
matters.text: Many large Roman groups have public shareholders or depend on public contracts. Clients entering joint ventures or supply relationships need to understand governance, political exposure, pending investigations and disputes. We research these from company filings, court and regulatory decisions and Italian media.

matters.title: Real estate and hospitality ownership
matters.text: Roman property, hotels and restaurants are often held through holding companies, fiduciary companies and family structures. We trace ownership from business register and land records, identify connected parties and prior proceedings, and assess any indications of illicit capital in a transaction.

matters.title: Tribunale delle imprese litigation support
matters.text: Shareholder, director liability and intellectual property disputes are heard by the specialised business section of the Tribunale di Roma, where cases can be lengthy. We support counsel with witness and party backgrounds, corporate histories and asset indicators that inform strategy and settlement.

matters.title: Asset research for enforcement
matters.text: Creditors enforcing judgments or awards against Rome-based debtors need to know what shareholdings, property and receivables exist. We map these from public registers and connected-entity research, so counsel can target attachment and other enforcement measures available under Italian procedure.

local_context.title: Tribunale di Roma business section
local_context.text: The Tribunale di Roma hosts a specialised business section created under Decree-Law 1/2012, which extended the existing intellectual property sections. It hears disputes involving joint-stock companies, their parents and subsidiaries, including shareholder disputes, challenges to resolutions and claims against directors and auditors, as well as IP and class actions. Its territorial reach extends beyond Lazio. A 2022 study found the section with about 8,000 pending cases and dispositions well above the national average duration.

local_context.title: Administrative and higher courts
local_context.text: Rome is the seat of the Court of Cassation, the Council of State and the Lazio Regional Administrative Tribunal (TAR Lazio), which hears challenges to many acts of national authorities, including procurement and regulatory decisions. For companies dealing with ministries and agencies, administrative litigation in Rome is often as important as civil litigation, and its decisions are a useful source for counterparty research.

local_context.title: Arbitration and mediation
local_context.text: Arbitra Camera, a special agency of the Rome Chamber of Commerce established under Law 580/1993, administers arbitration and conciliation for commercial disputes. Consob, also based in Rome, has operated a chamber for conciliation and arbitration for investor disputes. Italian and international parties may also choose other institutions or ad hoc arbitration seated in Rome. The forum and its rules affect how factual research must be organised and presented, so we agree the format with counsel at the outset.

local_context.title: Registers and chamber of commerce
local_context.text: Companies in Rome are registered in the business register kept by the Rome Chamber of Commerce, which provides official extracts showing directors, auditors, registered shareholders of limited companies, filings and financial statements. Property is recorded in the land registry and cadastre offices of the Revenue Agency for the Rome area. Together these sources support ownership and asset research, though fiduciary holdings can obscure ultimate owners.

local_context.title: National regulators in Rome
local_context.text: Rome hosts Consob, the securities regulator, the Bank of Italy, the insurance supervisor IVASS and ANAC, the national anti-corruption authority that oversees public procurement. Their published sanctions, decisions and registers are key sources when assessing Italian financial firms, listed issuers and procurement counterparties. Many of these registers can be consulted online, and decisions are often published with reasons, giving useful detail on the individuals and companies involved.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Rome and works on Roman matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client and Italian counsel first, whether a procurement bid, a state-linked joint venture, a shareholder dispute before the Tribunale delle imprese, an administrative challenge or enforcement, and scope the research to it. Sources include chamber of commerce extracts, land registry and cadastral records obtained lawfully, court and TAR decisions, regulator publications and Italian media. Any field enquiries in Italy are carried out by investigators holding a prefectural licence, within GDPR and Italian data protection rules for defensive investigations. Reports state sources and confidence so counsel can rely on them in Italian proceedings.

faqs.q: Which Rome court hears shareholder and director disputes?
faqs.a: Disputes involving joint-stock companies, including shareholder conflicts, challenges to resolutions and claims against directors and auditors, are generally assigned to the specialised business section of the Tribunale di Roma, created under Decree-Law 1/2012. Its territorial reach extends beyond Lazio. Counsel confirms jurisdiction; we tailor research to that court's procedure.

faqs.q: Where are procurement decisions in Rome challenged?
faqs.a: Challenges to tender procedures and other acts of national authorities are often brought before the Lazio Regional Administrative Tribunal in Rome, with appeals to the Council of State, also in Rome. Published decisions are a useful source on how a counterparty has performed in past tenders and whether exclusions or disputes have arisen.

faqs.q: Do investigators need a licence to work in Rome?
faqs.a: Yes. Private investigation in Italy requires a licence issued by the prefect under the Consolidated Law on Public Security. In Rome that is the Prefecture of Rome. TDSC does not hold an Italian licence and coordinates licensed Italian investigators, working with Italian counsel, for any local enquiries.

faqs.q: Can the owners of a Roman company be identified from public records?
faqs.a: Usually in part. The business register kept by the Rome Chamber of Commerce shows directors, filings and registered shareholders of limited companies, but shares may be held by fiduciary companies or foreign holding entities. We combine register data, financial statements, litigation and media to assess who ultimately controls the company and state our confidence.

faqs.q: Is there an arbitration institution in Rome?
faqs.a: Yes. Arbitra Camera, a special agency of the Rome Chamber of Commerce, administers arbitration and conciliation of commercial disputes. Parties may also choose other Italian or international institutions with a Rome seat, or ad hoc arbitration. We support counsel with factual research suited to whichever forum is chosen.
